laurent_bridge_lock.arbitrary_characteristic_zero: Let K be any characteristic-zero field. Generate L over Q by the finitely many map coefficients and finitely many generators of Gamma_0; L embeds in C. Every gamma in Gamma is algebraic over L, so extend the embedding of L to an algebraic closure containing the relevant points. Never assert an embedding of all of K.
laurent_bridge_lock.arbitrary_finite_rank: Choose gamma_1,...,gamma_r whose tensor classes form a Q-basis and put Gamma_0=<gamma_1,...,gamma_r>. For each gamma in Gamma, an integral rational relation gives gamma^N times a Gamma_0 element equal to a torsion element tau; killing the finite order of that individual tau gives gamma^(NM) in Gamma_0. Hence Gamma is contained elementwise in Gamma_0^div.
laurent_bridge_lock.arbitrary_torsion: No finite-generation or bounded-torsion hypothesis is allowed. The argument is elementwise and covers arbitrary infinite torsion, including mu_infinity; each torsion element has finite order and lies in the division hull of the identity.
laurent_bridge_lock.geometric_transfer: Absence of a positive-dimensional torus coset is preserved under the chosen field embedding, and injectivity transfers finiteness back.

part_a.theorem_name: Anchored torus-coset dimension decay and sharp finite-rank clock

part_b.arithmetic_conclusion: For every characteristic-zero K and finite-rank Gamma<=K* with arbitrary torsion, T_2 is finite off the {1,d} resonance and for every other nonlinear actual support; on the resonant {1,d} locus T_3 is finite. These are qualitative statements.
part_b.exceptional_support: If E={1,d}, d>=2, and P(X)=beta X+delta X^d, then V_2^0 contains a positive-dimensional connected torus coset if and only if a=-beta^2. On that locus the unique connected positive-dimensional coset is C_d={((delta/beta^2)t^d,t,beta t,delta beta^d t^d):t in G_m}. For every coefficient choice, including resonance, V_3^0 has no positive-dimensional torus coset.
part_b.field_and_parameters: Omega is algebraically closed of characteristic zero; k=2; nu=1; c=0; a is nonzero; P(X)=sum_(e in E)b_e X^e where E is a nonempty finite subset of positive integers, every b_e is nonzero, and E is the actual collected support.
part_b.geometric_arithmetic_separation: The existence of C_d does not imply infinite T_2(S,Gamma) for every Gamma. Compatibility is separate; beta=delta=1,a=-1,Gamma=<2> gives (t^d,t,t,t^d) and infinite T_2.
part_b.linear_support: If E={1} and P(X)=beta X, choose any nonzero root r of r^2=beta r+a. For every m>=0, {(t,rt,...,r^(m+1)t):t in G_m} is a one-dimensional torus coset in V_m^0, so no finite geometric rigidity window exists.
part_b.other_nonlinear_supports: For every nonlinear monomial E={d}, d>=2, every binomial E={p,q} with 2<=p<q, and every support with |E|>=3, V_2^0 contains no positive-dimensional torus coset. Consequently every nonlinear support has no positive-dimensional torus coset in V_3^0.
part_b.recurrence: x_(n+2)=P(x_(n+1))+a x_n; in particular x_2=P(x_1)+a x_0, x_3=P(x_2)+a x_1, and x_4=P(x_3)+a x_2.
part_b.survivor_variety: V_m^0 is the closed subvariety of G_m^(m+2), with coordinates x_0,...,x_(m+1), cut out by x_(n+2)=P(x_(n+1))+a x_n for 0<=n<m.
part_b.theorem_name: Exact zero-constant planar support and resonance phase
